meta.titre: International and Regional Organisations: who does what beyond our borders
meta.sous_theme: The United Nations, its courts and agencies, the Red Cross and African and regional bodies

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Citizenship Education past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: When floods or war force families from their homes, a Red Cross volunteer is often among the first to arrive with first aid and blankets. When two countries cannot agree about a boundary, they may ask a world court to decide, as Cameroon and Nigeria did, and the court gave its judgment in 2002. Cameroon belongs to many bodies that work across borders. Examiners like to test whether you can match an organisation to its job, so you must know what each one does.

items: A state is an independent country with its own government.
A treaty is a written agreement between states.
An international organisation is a group formed by states to work together on common problems.

sections.titre: International and regional organisations: purposes, organs and roles
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Why organisations are formed
Peace, disease, trade, human rights and the environment are problems that cross borders. States therefore form organisations to cooperate.

### The United Nations (UN)
The UN was founded in 1945, after the Second World War, to maintain international peace and security, to develop friendly relations among nations and to promote human rights and development.

| Organ | Main role |
|---|---|
| General Assembly | All members take part and each has one vote. It debates world issues and makes recommendations. |
| Security Council | It has the main responsibility for peace and security, with five permanent members and ten non-permanent members. It can authorise peacekeeping missions and sanctions. |
| International Court of Justice (ICJ) | The principal judicial organ. It settles legal disputes between states and sits at The Hague. |
| Economic and Social Council | It coordinates economic and social cooperation. |
| Secretariat | Led by the Secretary-General, it runs the daily work. |

UN agencies include **UNESCO** (education, science and culture), **WHO** (health), **UNICEF** (children), **FAO** (food and agriculture), **ILO** (labour) and **UNHCR** (refugees).

### The International Criminal Court (ICC)
The ICC is a permanent court created by a treaty and is separate from the UN organs. It tries **individuals** accused of the gravest crimes, such as genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes. It also sits at The Hague.

**Do not confuse them:** the ICJ settles disputes between **states**; the ICC prosecutes **persons**.

### The Red Cross
The International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement was founded by Henry Dunant, a Swiss, in the nineteenth century. Its principal role is to protect and help victims of war, armed conflict and disasters: first aid, relief, care of the wounded and tracing of missing family members. It is neutral and impartial. Cameroon has its own national society.

### Regional and other bodies
- **African Union (AU):** replaced the OAU in 2002; promotes unity, peace and development in Africa.
- **CEMAC** and **ECCAS:** bodies for economic cooperation and integration in Central Africa, to which Cameroon belongs.
- **The Commonwealth** and **La Francophonie:** Cameroon belongs to both.

variantes.nom: Matching an organisation to its role
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question gives a role and asks for the body
variantes.contenu_markdown: Memorise one verb per body: ICJ settles state disputes, ICC prosecutes individuals, Security Council keeps peace, WHO protects health, UNESCO promotes education and culture, Red Cross helps victims of war and disasters.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks you to compare or distinguish
variantes.contenu_markdown: State who the body deals with (states or persons), what it decides, and where it sits. Give one clear sentence for each body.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks how Cameroon or its citizens gain
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give separate benefits with a result: health programmes against disease, help for refugees, schooling support, peaceful settlement of disputes, regional trade and cooperation.

sections.enonce_markdown: Distinguish between the International Court of Justice and the International Criminal Court, and state one role of the Red Cross. (6 marks)

etapes.justification: Distinguish means that you must show a difference, not describe each body alone.
etapes.resultat_markdown: One sentence for each court, with a clear contrast.

etapes.justification: The most important contrast is between states and individuals.

etapes.action: Add the type of matter and the link with the UN.
etapes.resultat_markdown: ICJ: legal disputes and a UN organ. ICC: grave crimes and set up by treaty.

etapes.justification: Only one role is asked, so one precise role is enough.
etapes.resultat_markdown: To protect and help victims of war and disasters.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: The International Court of Justice is the main judicial organ of the United Nations, and it settles legal disputes between states, such as disagreements about a boundary. The International Criminal Court is a separate court created by treaty, and it tries individuals accused of the gravest crimes such as genocide and crimes against humanity. One role of the Red Cross is to protect and assist victims of war and disasters, with first aid and relief.

items.pourquoi_faux: Disputes between states are the business of the ICJ. The ICC tries individuals accused of grave crimes.
items.correction_markdown: Write ICJ for state disputes and ICC for persons accused of grave crimes.

items.erreur_markdown: "The Red Cross is an army that helps a country to win a war."
items.pourquoi_faux: The Red Cross is a humanitarian movement. It is neutral, takes no side and helps victims of war and disasters.
items.correction_markdown: Write that its principal role is to protect and assist victims, without taking sides.

items.erreur_markdown: "The African Union is a department of the United Nations."
items.pourquoi_faux: The AU is a regional organisation of African states. It is separate from the UN, although the two can cooperate.
items.correction_markdown: Say that the AU is a regional body that promotes African unity, peace and development.

items.erreur_markdown: "All members of the UN sit in the Security Council."
items.pourquoi_faux: All members sit in the General Assembly. The Security Council has fifteen members, of which five are permanent.
items.correction_markdown: Link all members to the General Assembly and keep the Security Council for peace and security.

items.erreur_markdown: "The UN is a world government that makes laws for every country."
items.pourquoi_faux: The UN is an organisation of independent states that cooperate. Member countries remain sovereign and are bound by the treaties that they accept.
items.correction_markdown: Describe the UN as an organisation for cooperation among states.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Write in full: ICC, UNESCO and AU. (b) State one role of any one of them.
items.solution_markdown: (a) ICC: International Criminal Court. UNESCO: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation. AU: African Union. (b) For example, UNESCO promotes cooperation in education, science and culture; the ICC tries individuals accused of grave crimes; the AU promotes unity and development in Africa. Award one mark for each correct expansion and one for the role.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the organisation that is best placed to deal with each case: (i) thousands of refugees arrive in a country after a conflict; (ii) two states disagree about the position of their common boundary; (iii) a disease spreads across several countries; (iv) a former army chief is accused of genocide.
items.solution_markdown: (i) UNHCR, the UN refugee agency (the Red Cross may also help with relief). (ii) The International Court of Justice. (iii) The World Health Organisation. (iv) The International Criminal Court. Award one mark for each correct organisation.

items.enonce_markdown: "Regional organisations are more useful to African countries than the United Nations." Discuss, giving two points on each side and a conclusion.
items.solution_markdown: In favour: regional bodies such as the AU, CEMAC and ECCAS understand local problems; neighbours are affected first by conflict and so act quickly; they promote trade and cooperation within the region. Against: the UN has more members and more resources; the Security Council has the main responsibility for world peace; UN agencies run health, education and refugee programmes in every region. Conclusion: both are useful and they work best together, since regional bodies act close to the problem and the UN brings wider support. Award marks for developed points on both sides and for a clear judgement.

items_markdown: The UN was founded in 1945 to keep peace, develop friendly relations and promote human rights and development.
The Security Council keeps peace; the General Assembly includes all members; the ICJ settles legal disputes between states.
The ICC is a separate court that tries individuals accused of genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes.
UNESCO, WHO, UNICEF, FAO, ILO and UNHCR work in education, health, children, food, labour and refugees.
The Red Cross protects and helps victims of war and disasters and takes no side.
The AU, CEMAC and ECCAS are African and regional bodies, and Cameroon also belongs to the Commonwealth and La Francophonie.
